title: RDS PostgreSQL: managed database, owned data model
outcome: Configure private connectivity, backups, failover expectations, and Rails connection limits.
benefits: Managed infrastructure tasks and supported backup/HA features.
drawbacks: Queries, pool limits, restore evidence, and consistency remain your work.
version: AWS SDK for Ruby v3 · service-specific setup · no cloud resources created automatically
cue: Managed infrastructure does not remove application data responsibility.

trace.title: Private DB access
trace.detail: RDS manages parts of database infrastructure, not your schema, query design, or business rules. You still choose engine/version, instance/storage settings, network, credentials, backup retention, maintenance, and application connection behavior.

trace.title: Follow one item
trace.detail:
Rails checks out a connection → network/TLS/authentication → SQL/locks → commit → connection returns to pool. Multiply pool size by web/worker process count before comparing with DB limits.

During failover, existing connections can break. The app needs bounded retry/reconnect behavior and must not retry a non-idempotent transaction blindly after an unknown commit outcome.

trace.title: Try the failure
trace.detail: Managed backups do not prove your restore time. More app replicas can multiply connections. Read-replica lag can look like a lost update to the user.
